test_title: PYST 51: SSC CGL 2024 - General Knowledge (Held On 10 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following options is the legislative organ of the Union government?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The legislative organ of the Union government is Parliament.
 
• Parliament is made up of the President, the Rajya Sabha, and the Lok Sabha: 
 
• Rajya Sabha
 
 
• Also known as the Council of States, this is the upper house of Parliament.
 
• It has 245 members, with 233 representing states and union territories and 12 nominated by the President.
 
• The Rajya Sabha is permanent and cannot be dissolved. 
 
 
 
• Lok Sabha
 
 
• Also known as the House of the People, this is the lower house of Parliament.
 
• It is a temporary house that can be dissolved if the party in power loses the support of the majority of the house. 
 
 
 
• President
 
 
• The President has the power to summon and prorogue either House of Parliament or to dissolve Lok Sabha. 
 
• Parliament is the supreme legislative body of India and the highest representative authority of the people.
 
• However, the Supreme Court can review Parliament's laws, and the President and Vice President are part of the Executive branch. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Judiciary
 
 
• Interprets laws, settles disputes, and administers justice.
 
• For example, the Supreme Court interprets laws and can declare them unconstitutional. 
 
 
 
• Legislative assembly
 
 
• Makes laws and procedures, and examines the administration and its resolutions. In a state with one house, it is known as the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha).
 
• In a state with two houses, the lower house is known as the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and the upper house is known as the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad). 
 
 
 
• Executive
 
 
• Implements the laws enacted by the legislature and enforces the will of the state. For example, the President enforces laws and has the power to veto legislation. 
 
 
• Separation of Powers in India: Executive, Legislature ...
 
• The separation of powers is the division of these functions among separate and independent bodies.
 
• The purpose of separation of powers is to limit the possibility of arbitrary excesses by the government
